title: Holding SPY only while the market was open lost money from 2001 to 2014, and holding it straight through made 45%
author: person-person12
selftext:
There's an old claim that nearly all of the S&P's gains happen overnight, so I tested the most literal version of it I could. Buy SPY on the first 5 minute candle after the 9:30 open, sell just before the close, every single trading day, and never hold a share overnight. January 2001 to April 2014, $10k starting.

**Market hours only:** 3,171 days traded, 44.8% of them green, and **down 9.9% before any costs**.

**Buy and hold over the same stretch:** $10k to $14,513, up 45%, with a 56% worst drop along the way through 2008.

So over those 13 years the part of the day most people actually watch lost money, and **everything SPY made came between roughly 3:55 in the afternoon and 9:35 the next morning**.

The costs dont change that, since the market hours version was already negative before a cent of them came out. I ran it in [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading) with $0.03 a share slippage and $0.50 commission on each side, which is on the heavy side for SPY tbh, and trading in and out 3,171 times paid $8,815 in costs on a $10k account. That took it down to $199 by April 2014, which is why the test stops there instead of running to 2026.

comments.author: profittoinvest
comments.body: An interesting observation. I like patterns like that; it is precisely thanks to observations of this kind that you can build cool algorithms for further testing.
